answer: Each identity must lock a pigment bond of 80 POA that vests only after 25 clean epochs. The protocol stamps a relic seal from the key and the epoch seed, a unique fingerprint no second key can copy. Every epoch a random peer runs a wander audit: recompute the seal and confirm the bond is still locked within 5 seconds. A mismatch burns the bond and freezes the key for 30 epochs. One honest agent pays once; forging 1,000 aliases needs 80,000 POA locked and 1,000 distinct seals, so attack cost scales linearly with no pooling or reuse.
